tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue growth drivers Q3 fiscal 2025

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue growth drivers Q3 fiscal 2025

**NVIDIA’s Data Center revenue reached a record $30.8 billion in Q3 FY2025** (quarter ended October 27, 2024), growing **17% sequentially and 112% year over year**. [[1]] 

The principal driver was **exceptional demand for the Hopper platform**, particularly the H200: H200 sales rose sequentially to **double-digit billions of dollars**, which NVIDIA described as the fastest product ramp in its history. [[2]]

**Hyperscale cloud-service providers (CSPs)** were the largest demand source, representing approximately **half of Data Center sales**; their revenue more than doubled year over year as they deployed H200 compute and high-speed networking for expanding AI-training and inference capacity. [[2]] [[3]] 

NVIDIA also benefited from broadening cloud demand beyond the largest hyperscalers: **GPU regional-cloud revenue doubled year over year**, with strength across North America, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific, including sovereign-cloud buildouts. [[2]]

**Consumer-internet companies more than doubled their NVIDIA-related spending year over year** as they scaled Hopper infrastructure, while enterprises increasingly deployed NVIDIA AI platforms for copilots and agents. [[2]] 

The growth mix extended beyond GPUs: **Spectrum-X Ethernet revenue increased more than threefold year over year**, and software, service, and support revenue was annualizing at **$1.5 billion**, supporting the broader AI-system and networking opportunity. [[2]] 

Finally, cloud availability helped translate demand into deployments: H200-powered instances were available through AWS, CoreWeave, and Microsoft Azure, with Google Cloud and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure expected to follow. [[1]] [[2]] 

In short, Q3 FY2025 Data Center growth was driven by the H200 ramp, hyperscaler AI infrastructure investment, regional/sovereign cloud expansion, accelerating inference and enterprise-AI usage, and increasing attach of networking and software/services. [[2]]

Sources:
[S4.1] NVIDIA Corporation - NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Third Quarter Fiscal 2025 — https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2024/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-Third-Quarter-Fiscal-2025/default.aspx

events.content:
**Summary of NVIDIA Data‑Center Revenue Findings (most recent fiscal quarters)**  

| Quarter (FY) | Reported Data‑Center Revenue | QoQ Growth | YoY Growth | Key Drivers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 FY2025 (ended Apr 2024) | **$22.6 B** | +23 % | +427 % | Hopper platform ramp‑up, early AI‑infrastructure demand, enterprise‑AI pilots |
| Q2 FY2025 (ended Jul 2024) | **$26.3 B** | +16 % | +154 % | Continued Hopper uptake, cloud‑service‑provider (CSP) expansion, networking‑attach (Spectrum‑X) |
| Q3 FY2025 (ended Oct 2024) | **$30.8 B** | +17 % | +112 % | H200‑product ramp (fastest in NVIDIA history), CSP‑led AI‑training & inference, regional‑cloud and sovereign‑cloud growth, enterprise‑AI adoption, software/services annualizing $1.5 B |

**Sources (traceable)**  
- Q1 FY2025: [S3.1] NVIDIA earnings release (https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2025)  
- Q2 FY2025: [S2.1] SEC filing (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581024000262/q2fy25pr.htm)  
- Q3 FY2025: [S4.1]‑[S4.3] earnings release, investor presentation, and earnings‑call transcript (https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2024/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-Third-Quarter-Fiscal-2025/default.aspx; https://s201.q4cdn.com/141608511/files/doc_financials/2025/q3/NVDA‑F3Q25‑Quarterly‑Presentation‑FINAL.pdf; https://finance.yahoo.com/news/nvidia-nvda-q3-2025-earnings-020011216.html)

**Growth‑driver synthesis**  
1. **Hopper‑platform (H100/H200) ramp** – each quarter the new GPU generation delivered the steepest revenue ramp NVIDIA has seen; H200 alone reached double‑digit billions in Q3 FY2025.  
2. **Hyperscale‑cloud demand** – CSPs accounted for roughly half of Data‑Center sales in Q3 FY2025, doubling year‑over‑year as they built out AI‑training and inference clusters.  
3. **Regional / sovereign‑cloud expansion** – GPU revenue in regional clouds and sovereign builds more than doubled YoY, spanning North America, EMEA, and Asia‑Pacific.  
4. **Enterprise‑AI adoption** – consumer‑internet firms and enterprises more than doubled spending on NVIDIA AI platforms for copilots, agents, and generative‑AI workloads.  
5. **Networking & software attach** – Spectrum‑X Ethernet revenue grew >3× YoY; software, service, and support revenue annualized at $1.5 B, broadening the AI‑system opportunity beyond GPUs.  

All figures are from the most recently reported fiscal periods and each claim is backed by an explicit source ID.
